headline: KSE-100 rebounds 369 points to 169,969 as IMF review optimism offsets a hawkish Fed hike to 3.75–4% and Brent holds near $98 on easing Hormuz flows
mood: Cautiously constructive · IMF talks offset a hawkish Fed and a lingering Hormuz risk premium

snapshot.label: Brent / WTI
snapshot.delta: Hormuz flows ease the risk premium

five_things.html: The KSE-100 opened firmly and surged as much as 1.12% intraday to a session high of 171,492.53 before late profit-taking pared gains, with the index settling at 169,969.33, up 368.92 points (+0.22%). Volume rose to 591.2 million shares (from 568.04 million) on traded value of roughly Rs20.2 billion, with advancers leading decliners 253 to 195 (47 unchanged) across 495 names. Sentiment was buoyed by expectations of progress in the IMF mission's fourth EFF review talks, the Finance Ministry's new Strategic Action Plan for the local-currency bond market, and a proposal allowing private firms to directly import LNG; HBL, Meezan Bank, Lucky Cement, Fatima Fertiliser, FFC, Engro Holdings, Engro Fertilizers, UBL, Systems and Mari Energies together added 467 points. TechJuice and Profit confirm the print.
five_things.sentiment: rebound stalls into the close, breadth positive

five_things.chip: Wall Street Diverges as Fed Hike Bites
five_things.html: US equities finished September mixed: the S&P 500 slipped 0.25% to 7,651.54 and the Dow fell 443.87 points (−0.86%) to 50,906.05, while the Nasdaq Composite edged up 0.24% to 26,861.06. For the month the S&P fell 0.5%, the Dow dropped 4.3% and the Nasdaq added 1.9%, as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.29% and the 2-year to 4.92% following the Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75–4% on 16 September — its first increase since July 2023 under new Chair Kevin Warsh. A funding deal signed 2 September keeps the government open through 11 December, removing a near-term shutdown risk. CNBC and Yahoo Finance confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: Oil Steadies Near $98 as Hormuz Flows Recover
five_things.html: Brent crude settled at $97.46 (the new front-month December contract closed at $98.03, +1.9%) and WTI at $90.60, holding well below mid-September's spike that followed Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline closure. Middle East crude exports hit roughly 16.3 million barrels a day in September — the highest since the war began in February — with Kpler estimating Hormuz throughput near 80% of pre-war levels; tanker insurance costs remain elevated and Tehran says it is ready for both defensive and offensive action if strait-reopening talks stall. Al Jazeera and Fortune confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: Gold, Silver Slip as Real Yields Bite
five_things.html: Bullion gave back part of September's rally: spot gold fell 0.60% to $4,168.01 an ounce and silver dropped 1.39% to $61.13, as a firmer dollar and rising real yields overwhelmed softer core inflation data. Kitco and Rio Times confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: SBP Holds at 11.5%, Rupee Steady as IMF Review Advances
five_things.html: The SBP's Monetary Policy Committee held the policy rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting on 14 September, balancing a cooling inflation trend — August CPI at 11.1% y/y, with brokerages pencilling September near 10.2–10.3% y/y (EST.) ahead of the PBS print — against persistent energy-price pressure. The rupee firmed a marginal Re0.01 to 277.11 interbank, while 3-month KIBOR held near 11.58/11.83 and 6-month at 11.80/12.05. An IMF mission under Iva Petrova began the fourth EFF and third RSF reviews on 23 September, with Finance Minister Aurangzeb holding a kick-off meeting on 29 September; a successful review could unlock roughly $1 billion under the EFF and $200 million under the RSF. Business Recorder and The Nation confirm the details.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's macro narrative turned cautiously constructive into month-end: the KSE-100 rebounded 0.22% to 169,969 as the government briefed the visiting IMF mission (fourth EFF, third RSF review, begun 23 Sep) and unveiled a Strategic Action Plan for the local-currency bond market alongside a proposal letting private firms directly import LNG. The SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% on 14 September for a third straight meeting, with August CPI at 11.1% y/y and September estimated near 10.2–10.3% y/y (EST.) by brokerages. The rupee firmed marginally to 277.11 interbank. Risks remain skewed to Gulf-linked oil costs and the pace of IMF disbursement, with 170,000 acting as the index's psychological pivot. The Nation and TechJuice.
matrix.gcc_html: Gulf fundamentals stayed split between resilient non-oil growth and a lingering Hormuz risk premium. Saudi Arabia's Riyad Bank PMI rose to 57.8 in September (from 56.4), a six-month high, as the Crown Prince's PIF 2026–2030 strategy doubled down on tourism, travel and entertainment to diversify away from crude. OPEC+ held its October output target unchanged at 31.1 million bpd, confirming the group has fully unwound its 1.65 million bpd of voluntary cuts, with a formal decision due at the 4 October meeting. Mid-September's Saudi East–West pipeline shutdown after drone strikes from Iraq, and UAE pump-price rises of up to 16.6% for October, underline that the Hormuz premium — even as flows normalise toward 80% of pre-war levels — has not fully unwound. Arab News and The National.
matrix.global_html: The Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75–4% on 16 September — its first increase since July 2023 under Chair Kevin Warsh — continues to reverberate: the 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.29% and the 2-year at 4.92%, both at multi-year highs, even as a 2 September funding deal keeps Washington open through 11 December. Equities closed September mixed, with the Nasdaq up on the month and the Dow down 4.3%. In trade policy, the EU's finalised framework with Washington locks in a 15% tariff on most EU exports to the US (with carve-outs for aircraft, generic pharma and scarce raw materials) while Section 232 steel and aluminium tariffs remain, keeping bilateral friction alive into year-end. Separately, the SEC's proposed 'Regulation Crypto Assets' framework is in public comment through 20 October, a step toward clearer digital-asset rules. CNBC and Supply Chain Dive.

legislative.policy_html: IMF Fourth EFF / Third RSF Review talks (from 23 Sep) plus a Finance Ministry Strategic Action Plan for the local-currency bond market and a proposal to let private firms import LNG directly.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: banks and primary dealers (deeper bond-market liquidity), LNG-reliant industry (import flexibility), fiscal credibility if the roughly $1.2bn combined tranche is unlocked. Loses: consumers if IMF-linked energy-tariff adjustments accompany the review; import-dependent sectors exposed to rupee volatility pending the staff-level agreement.

legislative.policy_html: Crown Prince-approved PIF 2026–2030 strategy prioritising tourism, travel and entertainment, alongside OPEC+'s decision to hold October output at 31.1m bpd.
legislative.sectors: Tourism & Entertainment, Sovereign Wealth, Energy, Shipping/Insurance
legislative.impact_html: Wins: PIF portfolio companies in travel, tourism and entertainment; non-oil exporters riding a six-month-high 57.8 PMI. Loses: shippers and insurers still pricing a Hormuz risk premium; motorists facing UAE pump-price rises of up to 16.6% in October.

legislative.policy_html: Finalised EU–US tariff framework locking in a 15% US tariff on most EU exports, with Section 232 steel/aluminium tariffs still in force.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: EU exporters of aircraft, generic pharma and scarce raw materials (MFN carve-outs); US importers of EU industrial goods, now tariff-free. Loses: EU steel and aluminium exporters still facing Section 232 duties, and general EU exporters absorbing the 15% baseline tariff.

levels.support_note: Tuesday's close; deeper support near 168,500 psychological floor
levels.resistance_note: Wednesday's intraday high; then 172,000 psychological resistance

desk_stance_html: The desk reads today's tape as a tactical bounce inside a wider risk-off regime, not a trend reversal: 169,969 keeps the KSE-100 pinned below the psychologically important 170,000 mark, and direction into Thursday hinges on three swing factors — the pace of the IMF fourth EFF review, the durability of the Hormuz de-escalation in oil flows, and whether US yields stabilise after the Fed's 16 September hike to 3.75–4%. We would fade strength into 171,000–171,500 and treat a daily close back below 169,600 as a resumption of the September downtrend. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 rebounds 369 points to 169,969 as IMF optimism offsets a hawkish Fed — but 170,000 is still proving sticky.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
Wall Street closed out September mixed: S&P 500 -0.25% to 7,651.54, Dow -0.86% (-443.87 pts) to 50,906.05, Nasdaq +0.24% to 26,861.06. The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.29% and the 2-year at 4.92% after the Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75-4% on 16 September — its first increase since July 2023 under new Chair Kevin Warsh. A funding deal signed 2 September keeps Washington open through 11 December. Gold slipped 0.60% to $4,168.01 and silver fell 1.39% to $61.13 as real yields bit into bullion. Brent settled at $97.46 and WTI at $90.60, well below mid-September's Hormuz-driven spike.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 surged as much as 1.12% intraday to 171,492.53 before late profit-taking trimmed gains to a close of 169,969.33, up 368.92 points (+0.22%) on volume of 591.2 million shares. Breadth was positive at 253 advancers to 195 decliners. The rally was driven by optimism around the IMF's fourth EFF/third RSF review (talks began 23 Sep), a new Strategic Action Plan for the local-currency bond market, and a proposal to let private firms import LNG directly. The SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting on 14 September; August CPI printed at 11.1% y/y, with September estimated near 10.2-10.3% y/y ahead of the official PBS release. The rupee firmed a marginal Re0.01 to 277.11 interbank.

GCC
Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI climbed to a six-month high of 57.8 in September as the Crown Prince approved PIF's 2026-2030 strategy, leaning further into tourism, travel and entertainment. OPEC+ held its October output target steady at 31.1 million bpd, confirming the group has fully unwound its voluntary cuts; a formal decision follows at the 4 October meeting. Mid-September's Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown after drone strikes from Iraq, and UAE pump-price increases of up to 16.6% for October, are reminders that the Hormuz risk premium hasn't fully cleared even as regional crude flows recover toward 80% of pre-war levels.

GLOBAL
The EU and US finalised a tariff framework locking in a 15% US tariff on most EU exports (with carve-outs for aircraft, generic pharma and scarce raw materials), while Section 232 steel and aluminium tariffs remain in place. Separately, the SEC's proposed 'Regulation Crypto Assets' framework is in public comment through 20 October.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
Pakistan: IMF review + local bond-market plan + LNG import liberalisation — wins for banks and primary dealers, risk for energy-tariff-exposed consumers.
GCC: PIF 2026-2030 strategy + OPEC+ output hold — wins for non-oil/tourism plays, risk for shippers and insurers still pricing Hormuz.
Global: EU-US tariff deal — wins for carved-out EU exporters and US importers, losses for EU steel/aluminium exporters.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 169,600 (deeper support 168,500) · pivot 169,969 · resistance 171,490 (then 172,000). Desk stance: a tactical bounce inside a wider risk-off regime, not a trend reversal — fade strength into 171,000-171,500 and watch for a close back below 169,600. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
